t: A pocket debugger that lets you pause and inspect code on tiny chips.
steps: Buy the V2.3 probe from 1BitSquared or Adafruit.
Install GDB for Arm chips on your computer.
Plug the probe into your computer with a USB-C cable.
Find the two new serial ports. One is the GDB port and the other is the serial link.
Connect the ribbon cable to the debug connector on your target board.
Start GDB and connect with the target extended-remote command and the GDB port.
Load a simple blink program and set a breakpoint inside the loop.
Update the probe firmware later with the bmputil tool.
meta: Open Board. From $74.95. A few stores.
